# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_003_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 3

**3:1** Looking up toward heaven, she saw a nest of sparrows in the laurel tree, and she made lamentation within herself, saying:

**3:2** "Woe is me — who gave birth to me? What womb brought me forth? For I was born a curse before the children of Israel. I have been reproached and mocked, and they have cast me out from the temple of the Lord.

**3:3** "Woe is me — to what am I likened? I am not likened to the birds of heaven, for even the birds of heaven are fruitful before you, O Lord.

**3:4** "Woe is me — to what am I likened? I am not likened to the beasts of the earth, for even the beasts of the earth are fruitful before you, O Lord.

**3:5** "Woe is me — to what am I likened? I am not likened to these waters, for even these waters are fruitful before you, O Lord.

**3:6** "Woe is me — to what am I likened? I am not likened to the earth, for the earth brings forth its fruit in its season and blesses you, O Lord."

---

## Translator's Note

Anna's lament takes the form of a fourfold comparison — to birds, beasts, waters, and earth — each one making the same devastating point: even the inanimate world is more fruitful than she is. This is one of the most formally beautiful passages in the Protevangelium, deliberately recalling the lament psalms. The nest of sparrows seen in verse 1 triggers the entire sequence.
